findings: Stock Chorus has nontrivial DSP init and sample-processing entries; its wet audio renders in the DSP-only host without a ColdFire audio routine.
Its init reads the stock instance allocator and places the second channel 1536 words after the first, fitting the 3072-word FX1 allocation.
The sample path uses a 1532-position modulo cursor with padded channel storage, up to five tap states per channel, DSP control smoothing and parallel ALU/memory moves.
Air Chorus retains independent 8192-word stereo rings and a different algorithm. Copying stock Chorus buffer lengths or processing would not preserve its entire existing sweep.
Stock DELAY, and the existing CPU Tape Echo implementation, use the post-FX2 ColdFire/DMA path. That path does not itself provide processing between FX1 and FX2.
limits: Static inspection plus existing DSP-only renders; no new physical hardware timing or CPU-port implementation.
Only addresses, hashes and original analysis are retained. Stock routine bytes/disassembly and memory dumps remain private.
